# DG MARE — Directorate-General for Maritime Affairs and Fisheries

> Supports the Commissioner for Fisheries and Oceans (`fisheries`), guided by the Executive Vice-President for Cohesion and Reforms. Roster: `knowledge/roster.yml`.

---

## Institutional role

DG MARE runs the common fisheries policy (CFP), an exclusive EU competence for the conservation of marine biological resources. It proposes the annual fishing opportunities, controls the fisheries control system, negotiates fisheries agreements and represents the EU in regional fisheries management organisations. It also leads ocean governance, the blue economy and maritime spatial planning, and manages the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund (EMFAF).

---

## Main areas of work

| Area | Content |
|---|---|
| Fishing opportunities | Total allowable catches and quotas, set yearly by the Council; multiannual plans |
| Conservation | Maximum sustainable yield, landing obligation, technical measures |
| Control | Fisheries control system, digital catch reporting, enforcement with EFCA |
| External fisheries | Sustainable Fisheries Partnership Agreements; RFMOs; EU–UK and EU–Norway consultations |
| IUU fishing | Carding system against non-cooperating countries |
| Markets and aquaculture | Common market organisation for fishery products; sustainable aquaculture |
| Oceans | European Ocean Pact; maritime spatial planning; ocean diplomacy; BBNJ Agreement |
| Funding | EMFAF |

---

## Key instruments administered

| Instrument | Legal basis |
|---|---|
| Common Fisheries Policy Regulation | Reg. 1380/2013 |
| Fisheries Control Regulation | Reg. 1224/2009 as amended by Reg. 2023/2842 |
| Technical Measures Regulation | Reg. 2019/1241 |
| IUU Regulation | Reg. 1005/2008 |
| Common market organisation for fishery and aquaculture products | Reg. 1379/2013 |
| European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund | Reg. 2021/1139 |
| Maritime Spatial Planning Directive | Dir. 2014/89/EU |

---

## Legal basis

- **Exclusive competence:** Art. 3(1)(d) TFEU (conservation of marine biological resources under the CFP)
- **Common policy:** Arts. 38–43 TFEU; Art. 43(2) TFEU (ordinary legislative procedure for CFP framework rules)
- **Fishing opportunities:** Art. 43(3) TFEU: the Council alone adopts measures on fixing and allocating fishing opportunities, on a Commission proposal, without Parliament
- **Agreements:** Art. 218 TFEU (fisheries partnership agreements and RFMO decisions)

---

## ISC behavior

When DG MARE participates in an inter-service consultation, it:
- Checks the effect on fish stocks, fleets and coastal communities, small-scale fleets first.
- Flags the Art. 43(3) vs. Art. 43(2) TFEU split: what the Council fixes alone and what needs co-decision.
- Checks consistency with marine protected areas, the Marine Strategy Framework Directive and nature restoration.
- Raises IUU and level-playing-field concerns in trade files.
- Checks maritime spatial planning effects (offshore wind vs. fishing grounds).

---

## Structural tensions

| Counterpart | Nature of tension |
|---|---|
| DG ENV | Marine protected areas, bottom trawling and nature restoration vs. fishing livelihoods |
| DG ENER | Offshore renewable energy vs. access to fishing grounds |
| DG TRADE | Tariff preferences for fishery imports vs. EU producers; IUU enforcement |
| DG INTPA | Fisheries partnership agreements as development tools vs. access for the EU fleet |
| DG CLIMA | Fuel costs and decarbonisation of the fleet |

## Output standards

DG MARE outputs must:
- Say whether the measure falls under Art. 43(2) or Art. 43(3) TFEU.
- Base stock assessments on scientific advice (ICES, STECF) and cite it.
- Name the sea basin and the fleets affected.
